summary:
Project SPROUTX is a climate-resilient crop rotation decision-support tool for smallholder farmers in Sri Lanka’s Dry Zone, built as a multilingual web app and installable PWA (Sinhala, Tamil and English). Farmers often choose crops without reliable information on soil moisture, rainfall or heat stress, and climate change makes those choices riskier. SPROUTX uses NASA Earth observation data, including SMAP soil moisture, GPM precipitation, NASA POWER weather, ECOSTRESS heat stress and SRTM terrain, together with local soil and crop information and each farmer’s priorities. It compares at least three rotation strategies, including the farmer’s existing one, and explains the evidence, benefits, information gaps and risks for each.

The interface is picture-based and voice-friendly for low-literacy users. It offers weather and heat alerts, AI pest and nutrient photo checks, chat with agriculture specialists, a fertilizer page, a farmer-buyer market and budget-based advice. To reach farmers with basic button phones, SPROUTX also provides SMS and call alerts through a sign-up form. The tool supports farmer judgment and local expert review rather than replacing them, helping improve soil health, water use and income under a changing climate.
details:
The problem
Smallholder farmers in Sri Lanka’s Dry Zone make planting decisions with little reliable data. Rainfall is becoming erratic, heat stress and water scarcity are rising, and soils are degrading. Wrong crop choices mean lost harvests, wasted fertilizer and lower income. Most existing agri-tech serves large farms and assumes smartphones, literacy and English.

Our solution
SPROUTX is a climate-smart crop advisor built for smallholders. It combines NASA satellite data (SMAP soil moisture, GPM rainfall, NASA POWER weather, ECOSTRESS heat stress, SRTM terrain) with local soil data, crop characteristics and each farmer’s budget and goals. It compares at least three rotation strategies, including the farmer’s current one, and for each it shows the evidence, benefits, risks and gaps. The farmer chooses what is best for their land.

Why it stands out

  • Built for real farmers: a picture-based, voice-friendly interface in Sinhala, Tamil and English.
  • Reaches everyone: SMS and call alerts for farmers with basic button phones.
  • Trusted advice: AI plus agriculture specialists, so local experts validate the recommendations.
  • All-in-one: rotation advice, pest and nutrient photo checks, weather and heat alerts, budget planning, fertilizer guidance and a farmer-buyer market.
  • Low cost to run: a Progressive Web App that works as a website and installs like an app, so there is no app-store dependency.

Business model (planned)

  • Fertilizer and input marketplace commissions
  • Farmer-to-buyer market and transport-matching fees
  • Partnerships with agriculture departments, NGOs and agribusinesses that fund farmer access
  • Premium analytics for larger farms and cooperatives

Impact
Better crop choices improve yields, save water and build soil health. That means higher, steadier income for farming families and more climate resilience for rural communities. The model can expand from the Dry Zone to the rest of Sri Lanka and to similar regions.

Technology
HTML, CSS and JavaScript PWA, a Python and GitHub Actions data and alert pipeline, GitHub Pages hosting and NASA Earth observation datasets.

Using Claude and gemini AI models.

Where we are and what’s next
We have built a working website with multilingual SMS alert sign-up and a prototype of the advice platform. Next steps are connecting live NASA data feeds, field-testing with Dry Zone farmers, and partnering with agriculture officers to validate the advice.
dataRefs: SMAP provides global measurements of surface soil moisture and freeze/thaw state, collected every 2–3 days. Soil‑moisture information helps identify drought stress, water availability, infiltration potential, and early crop‑stress signals. These data are valuable for evaluating rotation crops that could improve water efficiency, soil conditions, or drought resilience.

The GPM mission and its IMERG product provide global precipitation rate and accumulation estimates. These help assess rainfall reliability, extreme‑storm frequency, erosion risk, water input to soils, and long‑term trends in field moisture. IMERG is valuable for comparing rotation strategies under different precipitation scenarios.

Agroclimatology & Meteorological Data: NASA POWER provides accessible solar, meteorological, and climatology datasets used widely in agriculture. The datasets include temperature, humidity, radiation, and derived indicators that help estimate crop water use, growing‑season conditions, frost risk, and climate suitability for potential rotation crops.

Elevation & Terrain Models: The Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) provides global elevation data suitable for analyzing slope, runoff, erosion risk, water flow, and terrain‑driven stress conditions. Terrain patterns help determine which rotation crops may improve infiltration, reduce erosion, or stabilize soil on slopes.
